name: Danielle Ortiz

five_sec.what_is_it: dinner planner app, it texts the fam dinner ideas and puts the list in instacart or walmart
five_sec.who_for: families w/ older kids who have phones lol
five_sec.trust_why: says no card + powered by instacart badge, but never heard of it and no reviews up top
five_sec.next_step: tap 'see a sample week' to see if the dinners are actually fast
five_sec.delivers_food_why: the green line literally says 'We don't deliver food' right above the button

full_page.what_stopped_me: almost nothing, but the whole top part is about kids voting by text and mine are 5 and 17 months, they can't text. Thursday meatballs are 35 min, too long for us
full_page.whats_missing: a 'under 20 min' week that's the default, real food photos, and does Fry's work? It says Kroger only on the paid one

DD.quote: ok the sample week has chicken tenders, taco night and english muffin pizzas with times on every one. my 5yo would eat 4 of those 5 lol

five_sec.what_is_it: meal plan thing, there's a video of a mom and kid cooking
five_sec.who_for: moms who want less stress? kinda vague
five_sec.trust_why: looks like a real company but I can't tell what it costs and I'm not watching a video in the pickup line
five_sec.next_step: scroll for prices and prep times
five_sec.delivers_food_why: 'Less Stress, More Dinners' and a cooking video, nothing says if they send food or recipes

full_page.what_stopped_me: a pop-up asking for my email, no price anywhere, and the dinners shown are Pork Chops with Rosemary-Mustard Sauce and Plum-Watercress Salad. my kids would riot
full_page.whats_missing: the price and how long each dinner takes

EM.quote: plum-watercress salad?? on a tuesday with a toddler screaming? and I scrolled the whole thing and still don't know what it costs

five_sec.what_is_it: hellofresh, the box people, with a 'pick a mystery box' game in my face
five_sec.who_for: people w/ time to cook 40 min dinners
five_sec.trust_why: I know them, I used them, but 'open a box to reveal your offer' feels like a casino
five_sec.next_step: close the pop-up, honestly probably close the tab
five_sec.delivers_food_why: it's hellofresh, the boxes on screen, I literally got one in 2024

full_page.what_stopped_me: already did it, 'ready in 20 minutes' was 40 for me. prices hidden behind a zip code and a wall of fine print
full_page.whats_missing: actual prices without typing my zip

HF.quote: '30 minutes or less' lol. the cooking took me 40 and that's why I cancelled. not falling for the mystery box

five_sec.what_is_it: an AI app that picks dinner for you
five_sec.trust_why: 90,000 families sounds legit and the app pic is cute, but the big orange button is a 'Letter from the CEO'?? why
five_sec.next_step: scroll to see reviews and price
five_sec.delivers_food_why: the phone pic shows a menu and recipes, looks like an app not a box

full_page.what_stopped_me: the FAQ says prices are in the app and the pricing page is $25 a month. way over my $10. counting 'messages' is weird
full_page.whats_missing: prep times on the dinners and a normal price

OL.quote: love the 'working mom of a toddler' review but $25 a month to text a robot? and the button is a CEO letter lol who reads that

five_sec.who_for: people who already have a pile of recipes saved
five_sec.trust_why: 4.8 on the app store and 'no card required' right there
five_sec.next_step: probably leave, I don't save recipes
five_sec.delivers_food_why: says recipes, meal plans and grocery lists, all in one app

full_page.what_stopped_me: I have to bring my own recipes and do the planning. that's the part I can't do at 4:45

PTE.quote: it literally says 'an app for do-ers'. babe I am not a do-er at 4:45 in the car line

dd_offer.why: I saw 'no card' and 'Family free 14 days' but I skimmed and didn't get that Family is the paid version, I thought family = my family
dd_offer.expect_day_15: probably starts charging $4.99 unless I cancel, that's how these work lol

head_to_head.reason: only one that showed me real kid dinners with times and a price, free, no card

EM.reason: DD shows the week and the price, eMeals shows a video and fancy pork chops

PTE.reason: DD picks the dinners, Plan to Eat makes me do it

OL.reason: free vs $25 a month for basically the same idea

HF.reason: my own walmart groceries for $64 beats a 40-minute box

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page, first screen: lead with 'five dinners under 30 minutes your kids will eat' and the sample week photos with prep times, instead of the kids-vote-by-text pitch (my kids can't text); and say whether Fry's works on the free plan.
